ratings_why.fun: The mid game (Chimney, Wendelin, Gundel) is a real positional puzzle with a big late payoff, but at Tiers 1-3 most Gossips are too small to leave their unit, so the first turns play like plain self-buffers.
ratings_why.distinct: Gains that shrink as they travel along the zigzag, with you choosing where the news starts, play unlike any of today's tribes, though Hedgerow already owns touching-run growth.

verdict_why: The Winter Huddle loops as written and ties change the Knot in ways no card text states, so there are real fixes to make.

points.text: Each share counts as a hit on a unit in your Knot, so as written each share is split again, with no end. Say that shares aren't split again.

No keyword text says how a tie (or the Wheel of Heads' end link) changes who is in the Knot and how steps are counted. Put "tied units join the Knot; steps are the shortest path" into the Knot keyword.

At Tiers 1-3, Gossips like +2/+1 and +1/+1 reach a neighbour as +1/+0 or not at all, so the spreading idea only shows up at Tier 4. Make one Tier 1 or Tier 2 Gossip +2/+2 so that position matters from turn 2.
The Seconder's +1/+1 never leaves the Seconder, so it reads as a self-buff. Let it pass on half of what it heard instead, so it spreads when the news is big.
The Thirty-Two does nothing next to We, the Rattenkönig. Give it its own payoff, for example once a turn it Gossips the biggest amount it heard.

standouts.why: Mill-Chimney Voice turns positioning into the main decision, and doubled news travels one step further.
Speaker Brotkrume is a tall payoff for any tribe's big unit, and it rewards mixed boards.
Old Gundel is the moment the whole Knot grows at once, the turn you climb for.

weakest.why: The Seconder's Gossip is too small to spread, so it is a capped self-buff.
The Thirty-Two of Altenburg is a single receiver that the other Tier 6 makes redundant.
Cold-Shed Litter is a generic summon body that matters less once the board is full.

flags.note: As written, the shares split again and again without end (see p1). It also multiplies Bristle on every share.
With We, the Rattenkönig and Ilse, an Ooze eating a grown unit gives every unit about that unit's size each turn, and the next meal is bigger. That roughly doubles the board every turn.
With the Mill-Chimney and We, the Rattenkönig, every unit gains the biggest unit's full stats at Start of Combat. This lasts only the fight, but it decides the fight.
It doesn't say how a tie changes Knot membership or how steps are counted (see p2).
